In MDD, probiotic interventions and observational studies show significant associations with altered gray matter volume and functional connectivity in specific brain regions. For BD, observational studies suggest associations between gut-brain imbalance, immune activation, and prefrontal dysfunction.
key_finding_ja: 大うつ病性障害および双極性うつ病において、腸内細菌叢の変動が脳の構造的および機能的な変化と関連していることが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌叢の調整が、うつ病性障害における個別化医療のアプローチの一部として役立つ可能性が期待される。

title: Gut microbiome profiles as predictors of response to chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer.
abstract: This prospective cohort study investigates the predictive role of gut microbiota composition in determining the therapeutic response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) at Qiqihar Jianhua Hospital. A total of 178 patients underwent standardized CRT protocols and were stratified into responders and non-responders based on pathological tumor regression grades. Gut microbiome profiling was conducted via 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing and shotgun metagenomics at three treatment stages (pre-, mid-, and post-CRT). Responders exhibited significantly higher alpha diversity (Shannon, Chao1) at baseline and maintained greater microbial richness throughout treatment. Taxonomic analysis identified Faecalibacterium, Akkermansia, and Bifidobacterium as enriched in responders, while non-responders showed elevated Clostridium, Escherichia, and Streptococcus. Multivariate regression confirmed Faecalibacterium (OR = 1.16, P = 0.0002) and Akkermansia (OR = 1.27, P = 0.0146) as independent predictors of CRT response. Functional profiling revealed enrichment of anti-inflammatory pathways (butyrate synthesis, tryptophan metabolism) in responders and pro-inflammatory, stress-related functions (lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis, oxidative stress) in non-responders. Exploratory microbiome modulation using probiotics or fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) targeting Faecalibacterium and Akkermansia demonstrated increased responder rates by 12.5 and 18.2%, respectively. These findings highlight the potential of gut microbiome signatures as non-invasive biomarkers for CRT response prediction and as targets for adjunctive therapeutic strategies. Personalized microbiome-informed treatment may enhance CRT efficacy and reduce unnecessary exposure in non-responders, paving the way for precision oncology in rectal cancer.
authors: You J, Khan RM, Reji N.
screening_reason: The study investigates the predictive role of gut microbiota composition and diversity in determining response to chemoradiotherapy in rectal cancer.
summary_ja: 局所進行直腸がん（LARC）患者における術前化学放射線療法（CRT）への治療反応性と腸内細菌叢の関連を前向きコホート研究で調査した。治療反応群では、治療開始前および治療期間を通じて腸内細菌叢の多様性が高く、FaecalibacteriumやAkkermansiaなどの有益菌が豊富であった。多変量解析により、これらの細菌がCRT反応性の独立した予測因子であることが確認され、抗炎症経路の活性化とも関連していた。さらに、プロバイオティクスや糞便微生物移植を用いた探索的介入により、治療反応率の向上が示された。
summary_en: This prospective cohort study evaluated the gut microbiome as a predictor of response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in locally advanced rectal cancer patients. Responders maintained higher microbial diversity and enrichment of Faecalibacterium and Akkermansia, which were identified as independent predictors of CRT response. Exploratory microbiome modulation targeting these taxa demonstrated potential to increase therapeutic response rates.
key_finding_ja: 局所進行直腸がん患者において、FaecalibacteriumやAkkermansiaなどの特定の腸内細菌が術前化学放射線療法（CRT）の治療反応性を予測する独立した因子であることを明らかにした。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌叢を指標とした治療反応性の予測や、細菌叢の調整による治療効果の向上が、直腸がんにおける個別化医療の実現に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Grx2 deficiency accelerates BMSC senescence and senile osteoporosis via CD36 S-glutathionylation.
abstract: Rationale Senile osteoporosis (SOP) is driven largely by bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) senescence and mitochondrial dysfunction. S-glutathionylation is an important redox modification regulating mitochondrial homeostasis, yet its role in skeletal aging remains unclear. The objective of this study is to systematically investigate the role of Grx2 deficiency-mediated CD36 S-glutathionylation in BMSC senescence and SOP development. Methods Grx2, p53, and p21 expression in human and mouse BMSCs were analyzed by immunohistochemistry (IHC), western blotting (WB), and polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Aging-related and ovariectomy-induced osteoporosis models were established in Grx2 - / - mice for bone metabolism and senescence assessments. BMSC senescence, osteogenesis, and adipogenesis were evaluated by SA-β-Gal and WB, ALP/ARS staining, and ORO staining. Transcriptomic and S-glutathionylated proteomic analyses were performed to identify underlying mechanisms. Fatty acid uptake was quantified using two-color flow cytometry. DAG and MDA levels were measured to assess lipid overload and oxidative injury. Mitochondrial structure and function were evaluated by TEM, Mitotracker, qPCR, NAD + /NADH, ATP, ROS, JC-1, and Seahorse assays. The PI3K/AKT pathway was assessed by WB. Co-IP confirmed CD36 S-glutathionylation, and molecular docking predicted C272 as the key modification site. CD36-C272S mutation and Grx2 overexpression were applied to validate functional mechanisms in vitro and in vivo. Results Grx2 deficiency, in both male and ovariectomized female mice, accelerates bone loss, inhibits osteoblast formation without altering osteoclast function, and exacerbates BMSC senescence. Through integrated transcriptomic and S-glutathionylated proteomic analysis, we identified the fatty acid transporter CD36 as a critical downstream target of Grx2. Notably, Grx2 deficiency markedly increases the S-glutathionylation of CD36, which not only enhances its fatty acid uptake capacity, leading to the accumulation of toxic lipid metabolites and oxidative damage, but also impairs mitochondrial energy metabolism by inhibiting the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Overexpression of Grx2 or the C272S mutation in CD36, which disrupts its S-glutathionylation, can break this harmful cycle and inhibit BMSC senescence. Conclusions Grx2 deficiency-mediated CD36 S-glutathionylation drives BMSC senescence and SOP, providing new insight into the redox regulatory mechanisms underlying skeletal aging.
authors: Li M, Wumiti T, Sun J, Zhang T, Wang L, Zhou Q, Xia T, Shen J, Zhang Y, Ma Y, Guo Y.
screening_reason: The study investigates the role of CD36 S-glutathionylation, a covalent post-translational modification, in regulating stem cell senescence and osteoporosis.
summary_ja: 骨髄間葉系幹細胞（BMSC）の老化とミトコンドリア機能障害は、老人性骨粗鬆症（SOP）の主な要因である。本研究では、Grx2欠損がCD36のS-グルタチオン化を介してBMSCの老化とSOPを促進するメカニズムを解明した。Grx2欠損はCD36のS-グルタチオン化を増加させ、脂肪酸取り込みの亢進による脂質蓄積と酸化ストレスを引き起こし、PI3K/AKT経路を阻害してミトコンドリア代謝を損なう。Grx2の過剰発現やCD36のC272S変異は、この悪循環を断ち切りBMSCの老化を抑制した。
summary_en: This study investigates the role of Grx2 deficiency-mediated CD36 S-glutathionylation in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) senescence and senile osteoporosis (SOP). Grx2 deficiency increases CD36 S-glutathionylation, enhancing fatty acid uptake and causing lipid accumulation, oxidative damage, and mitochondrial dysfunction via PI3K/AKT pathway inhibition. Overexpression of Grx2 or a CD36 mutation (C272S) prevents S-glutathionylation and alleviates BMSC senescence.
key_finding_ja: Grx2欠損によるCD36のS-グルタチオン化の亢進が、脂質蓄積とミトコンドリア機能障害を引き起こし、BMSCの老化と老人性骨粗鬆症を駆動することを明らかにした。
why_it_matters_ja: 骨の老化における酸化還元修飾の役割が解明されたことで、老人性骨粗鬆症に対する新たな治療アプローチの開発につながる可能性がある。

title: From glycosylation to deglycosylation: Unraveling the complete deglycosylation processing pathway of Drosophila rhodopsin.
abstract: N-linked glycosylation is a prevalent post-translational modification during protein maturation, which plays a pivotal role in protein folding, stability, localization, and oligomerization. While the canonical pathway of N-linked glycosylation has been extensively characterized, the substrate specificities and regulatory functions of many carbohydrate-active enzymes as well as the context-dependent roles of protein-specific N-glycans in physiology and pathology remain to be fully elucidated. Drosophila rhodopsin1 (Rh1), which possesses a single N-linked glycosylation site and undergoes the complete removal of N-linked glycans during biosynthesis and maturation, serves as an optimal model for investigating the complex dynamics underlying N-linked glycosylation. Herein, we present a comprehensive analysis of the intricate N-glycan trimming of Rh1 and critically evaluate the molecular determinants driving its complete deglycosylation during maturation. We highlight the unique feature of complete N-glycan removal from Rh1, provide a detailed analysis of the key enzymes responsible for this process, and summarize the impact of aberrant N-linked glycosylation on Rh1 function. This narrative review aims to establish Rh1 as an excellent model for screening regulators of protein N-glycosylation and to provide a theoretical framework for understanding mammalian N-glycosylation.
authors: Chen X, Yuan Y, Zhong Y, Huang Y, Ouyang S, Xue Q, Qin Y, Hu X, Huang Y, Cao J.
screening_reason: The paper presents a detailed mechanistic analysis of N-linked glycosylation and deglycosylation, which are key protein post-translational modifications.
summary_ja: N結合型糖鎖修飾は、タンパク質の成熟過程における重要な翻訳後修飾である。本レビューでは、ショウジョウバエのロドプシン1（Rh1）の成熟過程における完全な脱糖鎖修飾経路を包括的に分析している。Rh1の糖鎖トリミングに関与する主要な酵素や、異常な糖鎖修飾がその機能に及ぼす影響をまとめている。Rh1をタンパク質糖鎖修飾の制御因子をスクリーニングするための優れたモデルとして提案している。
summary_en: This narrative review analyzes the complete N-glycan trimming and deglycosylation pathway of Drosophila rhodopsin1 (Rh1) during its maturation. It highlights the key enzymes involved in this process and summarizes the functional impacts of aberrant N-linked glycosylation. The authors propose Rh1 as an optimal model for screening regulators of protein N-glycosylation.
key_finding_ja: ショウジョウバエのロドプシン1（Rh1）の成熟過程における完全な脱糖鎖修飾経路と、それに関与する主要な酵素および機能的影響を明らかにした。
why_it_matters_ja: 本モデルは、哺乳類におけるN結合型糖鎖修飾の制御機構の解明や、関連する疾患の治療標的の探索に寄与する可能性がある。

title: From association to causality: mechanistic pathways linking the gut microbiome to psychiatric disorders.
abstract: The microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA) has emerged as a key framework for understanding how peripheral biological systems influence brain function and behaviour. However, despite extensive associative evidence linking gut microbiome to psychiatric disorders, robust causal and mechanistic insights remain limited. This review critically evaluates current evidence to determine whether microbiome alterations contribute to psychiatric pathophysiology and inform therapeutic strategies. We outline methodological frameworks for causal inference, highlighting the limitations of cross-sectional designs and the need for convergent evidence from longitudinal studies, experimental models, and human genetic approaches. We then synthesize mechanistic pathways linking the microbiota to brain function, including immune signaling, neuroendocrine regulation via the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, neural communication through vagal and enteric pathways, and intestinal and blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity. Across these systems, microbial metabolites and immune mediators emerge as key mediators, although direct causal mechanisms in humans remain incompletely established. Disorder-specific evaluation across major depressive disorder (MDD), anxiety disorders, bipolar disorder (BD), schizophrenia (SCZ), and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) reveals heterogeneous but converging evidence for microbiome involvement. Although preclinical and interventional studies support biological plausibility, human evidence remains constrained by confounding, variability, and limited mechanistic validation. Translational strategies, including psychobiotics, dietary interventions, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), and microbiome-based biomarkers, show promise but remain methodologically limited. Overall, the gut microbiome represents a biologically plausible and modifiable contributor to psychiatric disorders. Advancing toward clinical application will require integrative, longitudinal, and mechanism-driven research to enable precision psychiatry grounded in causal evidence.
authors: Almarzooqi S, Yassin LK, Alnuaimi F, Alketbi S, Skrabulyte-Barbulescu J, AlAhbabi N, Alremeithi D, Almarashda R, Almazrouei S, Shehab S, Statsenko Y, Hamad MIK.
screening_reason: The paper is a review focusing on the mechanistic pathways linking the gut microbiome to brain function and psychiatric disorders via the microbiota-gut-brain axis.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、腸内細菌叢と精神疾患を結びつける腸脳相関の因果関係および作用機序に関する現在の知見を評価している。免疫シグナル伝達、神経内分泌調節、神経伝達経路、およびバリア機能の維持といった主要な経路を整理しつつ、ヒトにおける直接的な因果関係の証明にはまだ限界があることを指摘している。また、サイコバイオティクスや糞便微生物移植などの臨床応用へのアプローチを議論し、今後の縦断的かつメカニズム重視の研究の必要性を強調している。
summary_en: This review evaluates the causal and mechanistic pathways linking the gut microbiome to psychiatric disorders through the microbiota-gut-brain axis. It outlines key pathways including immune signaling, neuroendocrine regulation, neural communication, and barrier integrity, while highlighting the limitations of current human evidence. The authors discuss translational strategies such as psychobiotics and fecal microbiota transplantation, emphasizing the need for longitudinal, mechanism-driven research.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌叢が精神疾患に影響を与える生物学的な妥当性を支持する経路を整理し、相関関係から因果関係の解明へと移行するための課題と展望を示した。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸脳相関を介した精神疾患の病態解明は、個別化精神医療や新たな治療法の開発に寄与する可能性があるが、臨床応用には因果関係を裏付ける強固なヒトデータの蓄積が必要である。

title: Disruption of mucosal immune homeostasis in food allergy: a convergence of genetic, barrier, microbiome, and environmental triggers.
abstract: Food allergy is a pathological immune response to food antigens. Its global prevalence continues to rise, making it a significant public health and food safety concern. This review describes the pathogenesis of food allergy, proposing that its development results from the interplay of multiple factors, including genetic background, disruption of the intestinal barrier, breakdown of oral tolerance, gut microbiome dysbiosis, and early-life environmental exposures. Genetic background establishes a baseline risk for the disease. Compromised intestinal barrier integrity facilitates abnormal allergen translocation and alarmin release, thereby initiating a type 2 immune response. The collapse of oral tolerance is marked by impaired regulatory T cell function and a dominant Th2 response. Gut microbiome dysbiosis, by altering key metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids, further exacerbates immune dysregulation. Dietary and environmental factors program these processes during critical early-life windows. Together, these elements form a dynamic, interactive pathogenic network. Future research should integrate multi-omics and systems biology approaches to better elucidate the interaction mechanisms within this network, thereby advancing the development of precise preventive and therapeutic strategies for food allergy.
authors: Zhang X, Gan D, Shi Y, Liu W, Yin H, Fu Q, Huang X.
screening_reason: The review discusses the pathogenesis of food allergy, focusing on the role of gut microbiome dysbiosis and mucosal immune homeostasis.
summary_ja: 食物アレルギーは食物抗原に対する病的な免疫反応であり、その世界的な有病率は上昇し続けている。本レビューは、食物アレルギーの発症が遺伝的背景、腸管バリアの破壊、経口免疫寛容の破綻、腸内細菌叢の乱れ（ディスバイオシス）、および初期の環境曝露の相互作用によって引き起こされると説明している。特に、腸内細菌叢の乱れは短鎖脂肪酸などの重要な代謝産物を変化させ、免疫調節不全をさらに悪化させる。これらの要素は動的かつ相互作用的な病原性ネットワークを形成しており、今後の多角的な解析が期待される。
summary_en: This review outlines the pathogenesis of food allergy, highlighting it as a complex interplay of genetic predisposition, intestinal barrier disruption, oral tolerance breakdown, gut microbiome dysbiosis, and early-life environmental factors. It emphasizes how gut dysbiosis alters key metabolites like short-chain fatty acids, thereby exacerbating immune dysregulation. The authors suggest that integrating multi-omics and systems biology will be crucial for developing precise preventive and therapeutic strategies.
key_finding_ja: 食物アレルギーの発症は、遺伝的要因、腸管バリア破壊、経口免疫寛容の破綻、短鎖脂肪酸などの代謝産物変化を伴う腸内細菌叢の乱れ、および環境要因が相互に作用するネットワークによって規定されている。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌叢やバリア機能を含む多角的な相互作用ネットワークを解明することは、食物アレルギーの新たな予防法や個別化治療法の開発に貢献する可能性がある。

title: EXPRESS: The Role of Complement System in Hemorrhagic Stroke.
abstract: Hemorrhagic stroke, including subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), and intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), is associated with high morbidity and mortality driven by secondary injury processes such as neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption, and oxidative stress. Increasing evidence identifies the complement system as a central mediator of these responses. Following hemorrhage, exposure of blood components and damaged tissue rapidly activates the classical, lectin, and alternative complement pathways, converging on C3 and leading to generation of anaphylatoxins and terminal effector complexes. In SAH, complement activation is early and compartmentalized, contributing to early brain injury, delayed cerebral ischemia, and vascular dysfunction. In ICH, complement exhibits dual roles, promoting inflammatory injury and edema while also facilitating hematoma clearance. In IVH, emerging data implicate complement in hydrocephalus development, white matter injury, and long-term neurological deficits, particularly via C3-mediated inflammation and membrane attack complex-driven hemolysis. Complement-coagulation crosstalk further amplifies injury through reciprocal activation pathways. Although complement-targeted therapies show promise in preclinical and early clinical studies, translation is limited by the dynamic and context-dependent nature of complement signaling. Future work should focus on biomarker development and precision therapeutic strategies.
authors: Wan Y, Reddi P, Fox A, Hua Y, Pandey AS, Keep RF, Koduri S.
journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
screening_reason: The review focuses on the role of the complement system in driving secondary injury processes, particularly neuroinflammation, following hemorrhagic stroke.
summary_ja: 出血性脳卒中（くも膜下出血、脳内出血、脳室内出血）は、神経炎症や血液脳関門の破壊などの二次的損傷プロセスにより、高い罹患率と死亡率を引き起こす。補体系はこれらの反応の中心的な媒介因子であり、出血後に古典的、レクチン、代替経路が急速に活性化される。くも膜下出血では早期脳損傷や遅発性脳虚血に関与し、脳内出血では炎症性損傷と血腫除去という二面性を示し、脳室内出血では脳室拡大や白質損傷に関与する。補体系を標的とした治療法は前臨床段階で有望視されているものの、その動的で文脈依存的な性質が臨床応用の課題となっている。
summary_en: This review highlights the complement system as a central mediator of secondary brain injury, including neuroinflammation and blood-brain barrier disruption, following hemorrhagic stroke. It details how complement activation contributes to early brain injury in subarachnoid hemorrhage, plays dual roles in intracerebral hemorrhage, and drives white matter injury and hydrocephalus in intraventricular hemorrhage. Despite the promise of complement-targeted therapies in preclinical models, their clinical translation remains limited by the dynamic nature of complement signaling.
key_finding_ja: 補体系は出血性脳卒中後の二次的脳損傷（神経炎症や血液脳関門破壊など）を媒介する中心的な因子であり、病態や出血部位に応じて多様かつ動的な役割を果たしている。
why_it_matters_ja: 補体系の複雑な活性化メカニズムを解明しバイオマーカーを開発することは、出血性脳卒中に対する精密な標的治療法の確立に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Diet-induced obesity fails to prime tumour-associated neuroinflammation in mice with Lewis Lung Carcinoma.
abstract: As obesity rates rise throughout the world and, given that obesity increases cancer risk for many forms of cancer, we can expect the rates of comorbid obesity and cancer to also rise. While obesity increases cancer-related symptoms including fatigue, depression, and neuropathy, the mechanisms underlying this exacerbation are understudied. As cancer and obesity have both been associated with alterations in neuroinflammatory processes, we used a murine model to investigate the interaction between cancer and obesity-associated neuroinflammation. We hypothesized that diet-induced obesity would result in neuroinflammatory priming and exacerbate tumour-associated neuroinflammation. Across 3 experiments, we evaluated the effect of diet in both male and female C57BL6J mice and tested two different diet durations: (1) 9 weeks of 45% High-Fat Diet (HFD) in female mice, (2) 9 weeks of 45% HFD in male mice, and (3) 24 weeks of 45% HFD with 10% fructose water in male mice. Mice on HFD and Standard Diet (SD) were randomized to receive either an injection of Lewis Lung Carcinoma (LLC) cells or PBS vehicle subcutaneously into the flank. After tumors were allowed to grow for approximately 3 weeks, tissue was collected and proinflammatory cytokine expression was evaluated in the hippocampus and hypothalamus. Overall, our results indicate that while long-term HFD consumption led to poorer health outcomes (as measured by faster tumor growth, enhanced weight loss, and greater spleen weights), it failed to prime the neuroinflammatory response to tumors.
authors: Fowler CG, Rodriguez R, Beaudry AG, Kusumo LE, Gillett AE, Wiggs MP, Law ML, Vichaya EG.
screening_reason: The study investigates the interaction between diet-induced obesity and tumor-associated neuroinflammation in a mouse model.
summary_ja: 肥満とがんの併存率が上昇する中、肥満ががん関連症状を悪化させる神経炎症メカニズムは十分に解明されていない。本研究では、高脂肪食（HFD）による肥満が、ルイス肺癌（LLC）を移植したマウスの腫瘍随伴性神経炎症を増悪させるか検証した。雌雄のマウスを用いて異なる期間のHFD摂取を行い、海馬および視床下部における炎症性サイトカインの発現を評価した。その結果、長期のHFD摂取は腫瘍成長の促進や体重減少などの健康悪化をもたらしたものの、腫瘍に対する神経炎症反応をプライミング（増強）することはなかった。
summary_en: This study investigated whether diet-induced obesity primes tumor-associated neuroinflammation in a murine model of Lewis Lung Carcinoma. Although long-term high-fat diet consumption led to poorer health outcomes, including accelerated tumor growth and increased weight loss, it did not exacerbate or prime the neuroinflammatory response in the hippocampus or hypothalamus. These findings suggest that the systemic effects of obesity on tumor progression may occur independently of tumor-associated neuroinflammatory priming.
key_finding_ja: 高脂肪食誘発性肥満は、ルイス肺癌マウスにおいて腫瘍の成長や体重減少を悪化させたものの、脳内（海馬および視床下部）の腫瘍随伴性神経炎症反応を増強することはなかった。
why_it_matters_ja: 肥満ががん患者の症状を悪化させるメカニズムにおいて、神経炎症のプライミング以外の経路が関与している可能性を示唆しており、今後の病態解明に寄与するかもしれない。

title: Comorbidity Between Mood Disorders and Chronic Somatic Diseases, With a Focus on Cardiometabolic Disease, and Its Mechanistic Crosstalk.
abstract: The comorbidity of mood disorders (MDs), represented by depression and anxiety, with chronic somatic diseases (CDs), particularly cardiometabolic conditions, poses a significant global public health challenge, markedly increasing the risk of adverse prognoses and all-cause mortality. Epidemiological studies indicate that ~36% of patients with multimorbidity exhibit psychosomatic comorbidity, with higher risk populations concentrated among females, older adults, and socioeconomically disadvantaged individuals. This review systematically analyzes the epidemiological distribution patterns of MD-CD comorbidity, with the strongest emphasis on cardiometabolic diseases-diabetes, metabolic syndrome (MetS), obesity, hypertension (HTA), and cardiovascular disease (CVD)-for which the mechanistic data are most developed, while also addressing osteoarthritis, psoriasis, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), cancer, and neurological disorders. By integrating molecular mechanisms with clinical evidence, we highlight core pathological pathways and critically evaluate the strength of evidence supporting each: hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis dysfunction and insulin resistance (IR), substantiated by clinical data and Mendelian randomization; NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated neuroinflammation as a transdiagnostic inflammatory node; gut-brain axis dysregulation involving bile acid-GLP-1 signaling and gut-derived metabolites such as trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO); and the kynurenine pathway (KP) as a branched metabolite axis with organ-specific consequences. Sex-specific mechanisms, particularly estrogen-regulated neuroendocrine and metabolic pathways, are identified as consistent biological modifiers of this comorbidity. A bidirectional vicious cycle underpins MD-CD comorbidity: metabolic abnormalities exacerbate limbic system dysfunction via HPA-axis hyperactivity, neuroinflammatory cascades, and disrupted gut-brain signaling, while MDs aggravate metabolic dysregulation through neuroendocrine disturbances and reduced treatment adherence.
authors: Du H, Du G, Zhang Q, Zhao Y, Fan J, Zhou Y, Sun Z, Li C, Li W.
screening_reason: The review details the mechanistic crosstalk of mood disorders and somatic diseases, focusing on neuroinflammation and gut-brain axis dysregulation.
summary_ja: 気分障害（うつ病や不安症など）と心代謝疾患などの慢性身体疾患との併存は、予後不良や全死因死亡率の上昇をもたらす重大な公衆衛生上の課題である。本レビューは、これら併存疾患の疫学的パターンを分析し、その根底にある分子メカニズムを体系的に評価している。具体的には、視床下部-下垂体-副腎（HPA）軸の機能不全、NLRP3インフラマソームを介した神経炎症、腸脳相関の乱れ、キヌレニン経路などが主要な病理学的経路として挙げられている。さらに、エストロゲンが調節する神経内分泌経路などの性差特異的なメカニズムも、この併存関係を修飾する要因として同定されている。
summary_en: This review systematically analyzes the epidemiological patterns and molecular mechanisms underlying the comorbidity between mood disorders and chronic somatic diseases, particularly cardiometabolic conditions. It highlights key pathological pathways, including HPA-axis dysfunction, NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated neuroinflammation, gut-brain axis dysregulation, and the kynurenine pathway. Additionally, the review emphasizes a bidirectional vicious cycle where metabolic abnormalities and mood disorders mutually exacerbate each other through neuroendocrine and inflammatory cascades.
key_finding_ja: 気分障害と慢性身体疾患の併存は、HPA軸の機能不全、神経炎症、腸脳相関の乱れ、キヌレニン経路などの複数の経路を介した双方向の悪循環によって維持されている。
why_it_matters_ja: これらの分子メカニズムを解明することは、精神疾患と身体疾患を併発する患者に対する、より効果的な統合的治療戦略の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Chronic kidney disease‑associated encephalopathy: Clinical features, pathomechanisms and emerging therapeutic strategies (Review).
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a progressive disorder whose systemic effects extend to the central nervous system, leading to CKD‑associated encephalopathy. Epidemiological data indicate that the prevalence of cognitive impairment in patients with CKD is as high as 40%, while mood disorders such as depression and anxiety exceed 60% among those receiving hemodialysis, and the risk of cerebrovascular events is also notably increased. These complications substantially impair the quality of life of patients, functional independence and long‑term prognosis, thereby constituting a considerable clinical burden. The key pathological mechanisms involve disruption of the 'gut‑kidney‑brain axis'. Declining renal function leads to the accumulation of gut microbiota‑derived uremic toxins, such as indoxyl sulfate, p‑Cresyl sulfate and trimethylamine N‑oxide. Through multiple pathways, including disruption of blood‑brain barrier integrity, induction of neuroinflammation, promotion of oxidative stress and direct neurotoxicity, these toxins collectively contribute to the injury of the neurovascular unit, neuronal dysfunction and even neurodegeneration. The present review systematically outlines the clinical manifestations, the aforementioned core pathogenic mechanisms and emerging therapeutic strategies for CKD‑associated encephalopathy. Clinically, early identification of neurological complications (such as through neuropsychological assessment, gait analysis and neuroimaging), along with monitoring of specific biomarkers, is crucial for timely intervention and improved prognosis. In terms of treatment, the targeted interventions on the gut‑kidney‑brain axis (such as specific probiotics and intestinal adsorbents), and the advantages and disadvantages of stem cells and gene therapy are summarized in the present review. A deeper understanding of these mechanisms will provide a solid theoretical foundation for the development of innovative treatments and ultimately improve neurological outcomes in patients with CKD.
authors: Zeng N, Jiang L, Zhang Y, Liu J, Zhang Q, Liao L, Hu Q.
screening_reason: The review focuses on the gut-kidney-brain axis, specifically how gut microbiota-derived uremic toxins induce neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment.
summary_ja: 本総説は、慢性腎臓病（CKD）に伴う脳症の臨床的特徴と、「腸・腎・脳軸」の破綻を中心とした病態生理学的メカニズムをまとめています。腎機能低下に伴って蓄積する腸内細菌由来の尿毒症毒素が、血液脳関門の破壊、神経炎症、酸化ストレス、および直接的な神経毒性を引き起こす機序を説明しています。さらに、プロバイオティクスや腸管吸着剤など、この軸を標的とした新たな治療戦略についても概説しています。
summary_en: This review outlines the clinical features and pathological mechanisms of chronic kidney disease (CKD)-associated encephalopathy, focusing on the disruption of the gut-kidney-brain axis. It describes how the accumulation of gut microbiota-derived uremic toxins leads to blood-brain barrier disruption, neuroinflammation, and neurotoxicity. The authors also summarize emerging therapeutic strategies, including probiotics and intestinal adsorbents targeting this axis.
key_finding_ja: 慢性腎臓病に伴う脳症の主たる病態として、腸内細菌由来の尿毒症毒素の蓄積による「腸・腎・脳軸」の破綻が関与していることを体系的に整理しました。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌叢やその代謝産物を標的とした治療介入が、慢性腎臓病患者における認知機能障害や精神症状の改善に寄与する可能性があります。

title: Estrogen's Master Switch: NFκB-NLRP3, SIRT1-HMGB1, and TLR4 Triad Tamed for Brain Rescue in Ageing and Neurodegeneration.
abstract: Estrogen operates as a pleiotropic steroidal, neuroendocrine modulator to combat accelerated brain ageing and neurodegeneration by addressing a convergent inflammatory-metabolic trio. Estrogen receptor-dependent neural cellular signalling reduces TLR4-mediated immune priming and NF-κB activation, preventing NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and pro-inflammatory cytokine release. Concurrently, estrogen increases SIRT1 activity, restoring metabolic and epigenetic equilibrium while inhibiting HMGB1 acetylation, translocation, extracellular release, and activation of the stress-response pathway. Coordinated regulation of the TLR4-NFκB-NLRP3 and SIRT1-HMGB1 molecular triad reduces chronic neuroinflammation, preserves neuronal integrity, metabolic resilience, and slows persistent inflammation-driven brain ageing. This highlights estrogen and estrogen-based steroidal modulators as promising therapeutic candidates for reversing accelerated cognitive ageing and neurodegenerative disorders. However, a crucial research gap persists in the absence of a systems-level assessment of neurosteroids as a multi-target regulator of convergent innate immunological and metabolic signalling networks. The control of the TLR4-NFκB-NLRP3 inflammasome axis and the SIRT1-HMGB1 metabolic-epigenetic checkpoint has not been well studied as an interrelated, steroidal druggable trifecta driving brain homeostasis and neurodegeneration. These pathways are often studied in isolation, despite overwhelming evidence that their bidirectional interplay contributes to persistent neuroinflammation, immunometabolic dysfunction, and cellular senescence. This review synthesises evidence from molecular endocrinology, biochemical, pre-clinical, and clinical models to advance a mechanistically integrated and therapeutically actionable framework that aligns into a unified endocrine, metabolic, and immune target-driven framework relevant to complex, inflammation-driven brain ageing, thereby offering a strong foundation and paving the way for future molecular target validation and disease-modifying, steroid-mimetic interventions against neurodegeneration.
authors: Shandilya A, Giri CK, Arwind DA, Ravichandiran V, Singh S, Parihar VK.
journal: The Journal of steroid biochemistry and molecular biology
screening_reason: The paper is a comprehensive review focusing on the molecular mechanisms of estrogen in reducing chronic neuroinflammation and preserving brain homeostasis.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、エストロゲンが脳の老化や神経変性疾患に対抗する神経内分泌調節因子として機能する機序に関する証拠をまとめている。エストロゲンはTLR4-NFκB-NLRP3経路とSIRT1-HMGB1経路の協調的な制御を介して、慢性的な神経炎症を抑制し神経細胞の完全性を維持する。著者らは、これらの相互に関連する免疫・代謝ネットワークを標的とした、神経変性に対する新たな治療的枠組みを提案している。
summary_en: This review synthesizes evidence on how estrogen acts as a neuroendocrine modulator to combat brain aging and neurodegeneration. Estrogen coordinates the regulation of the TLR4-NFκB-NLRP3 and SIRT1-HMGB1 pathways, thereby reducing chronic neuroinflammation and preserving neuronal integrity. The authors propose an integrated framework to target these interconnected immunological and metabolic networks for therapeutic interventions.
key_finding_ja: エストロゲンがTLR4-NFκB-NLRP3およびSIRT1-HMGB1の分子経路を協調的に制御することで、神経炎症を抑制し脳の恒常性を維持する仕組みが明らかになった。
why_it_matters_ja: エストロゲン様作用を持つ調節因子の活用が、加齢に伴う認知機能低下や神経変性疾患の進行を遅らせる新たな治療戦略となる可能性がある。

title: Glycosylation penetrance of N-X-S/T sequons in antibody variable domains: a structural survey of 19,265 human antibody structures reassessing the histidine/glutamine suppression hypothesis.
abstract: Machine learning (ML) approaches for de novo antibody design generate thousands of candidate sequences, but most lack a robust assessment of post-translational modification liabilities. N-linked glycosylation in variable domains can fundamentally alter antibody function, yet current penetrance estimates are derived from glycosylation-enriched datasets inflating risk estimates. We surveyed 19,265 human antibody structures from the Protein Data Bank (PDB), identifying 1,368 N-X-S/T sequons in variable domains (this study) with 7.82% observed penetrance (107/1,368; Wilson 95% CI 6.5-9.4%) - a crystallographic lower bound reflecting selection against glycosylated structures in the PDB - compared with 16.47% from a previously published glycosylation-enriched corpus. At the X-position, no glycosylation was observed at histidine (0/61; Wilson 95% upper bound 5.9%), lysine (0/26; upper bound 12.9%), or tryptophan (0/26), consistent with suppression. Glutamine showed 6.45% penetrance (2/31), indistinguishable from baseline and refuting its prior classification as a suppressor. Variable light domains showed higher aggregate penetrance than variable heavy (9.62% vs 6.79%; Fisher OR = 1.46, p = 0.075), though this contrast did not survive joint Bayesian adjustment. Regionally, FR2 was glycosylation-resistant (0/119) while FR1 (14.0%) and FR4 (12.1%) showed elevated rates. N-X-T sequons were 3.84-fold more susceptible than N-X-S in aggregate (13.64% vs 3.55%; Fisher exact p = 8.13 × 10 -12 , OR = 4.29). An independent PDB-overlap-free validation subset ( n = 449, 33 glycosylation events, 189 nonoverlapping PDBs) reproduced the central findings. Leakage-corrected Bayesian logistic regression confirmed the N-X-T preference as the most prior-stable effect and identified strong negative coefficients for proline and aromatic residues at the +3 position immediately C-terminal to the sequon; the histidine effect at the X-position was borderline under prior sensitivity. We present a confidence-interval-aware decision tree that integrates X-position, third-position, chain type, and regional context as a sequence-only triage instrument for ML-designed antibody candidates.
authors: Gaughan CL.
screening_reason: The paper presents a structural survey and analysis of N-linked glycosylation, a major protein post-translational modification, in antibody variable domains.
summary_ja: 本研究は、19,265個のヒト抗体構造を調査し、可変領域におけるN-X-S/T配列のN型糖鎖修飾の透過率を評価した。全体の透過率は7.82%であり、N-X-T配列はN-X-S配列よりも糖鎖修飾を受けやすいことが示された。また、X位置におけるヒスチジン、リシン、トリプトファンによる修飾抑制が確認された一方で、グルタミンが抑制因子であるという従来の説は否定された。
summary_en: This study analyzed 19,265 human antibody structures to evaluate the N-linked glycosylation penetrance of N-X-S/T sequons in variable domains. The overall observed penetrance was 7.82%, with N-X-T sequons being significantly more susceptible to glycosylation than N-X-S sequons. The findings confirmed glycosylation suppression by histidine, lysine, and tryptophan at the X-position, but refuted the prior classification of glutamine as a suppressor.
key_finding_ja: ヒト抗体可変領域におけるN型糖鎖修飾の実際の透過率は7.82%であり、X位置の特定のアミノ酸による抑制効果やN-X-T配列の高い感受性が明らかになった。
why_it_matters_ja: 機械学習を用いて設計された抗体医薬品候補の糖鎖修飾リスクを正確に評価し、効率的なスクリーニングを行うための有用なツールとなることが期待される。

title: Enhancing Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Immunotherapy under Stress through Sympathetic Nerve-T cell Interaction Blockade via Co-delivery of β-Blockers and aTIM-3 with Ultrasound-Responsive Bionic Nanoparticles.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), a refractory cold tumor, is characterized by a dense extracellular matrix (ECM) and stress-triggered neuroimmune crosstalk, which cause T cell exhaustion and poor efficacy of anti-T cell immunoglobulin and mucin domain-3 antibody (aTIM-3) monotherapy. Here, we report a sucrose-hybridized, Pan02 pancreatic tumor cell membrane-coated ultrasound (US)-responsive biomimetic nanocarrier (CT@SM) co-loading carvedilol (β-blocker) and aTIM-3. The Pan02 tumor cell membrane shell enables homologous tumor targeting, prolonged circulation, and reduced off-target distribution, while intercalated sucrose modulates vesicle acoustic impedance to generate US-triggered inertial cavitation. US activates cavitation to disrupt the ECM and co-releases cargos deep in tumors: carvedilol relieves norepinephrine-mediated T cell exhaustion, and aTIM-3 suppresses M2-type tumor-associated macrophages. Consequently, compared to free aTIM-3, up to an 11.23-fold increase of aTIM-3 in the tumor region was obtained in the CT@SM + US group. Immunotherapy efficacy was significantly enhanced by reactivating T cells, leading to suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival in the PDAC mice stress model. Overall, this study offers a promising strategy based on a dual-modified biomimetic acoustic delivery platform for immunotherapy in PDAC and other cold tumors.
authors: Li W, Zhang L, Li T, Yun Z, Ge M, Teng B, Feng T, Miao M, Dai Y, Li K, Liu F, Dong L, Ma T.
screening_reason: The study investigates sympathetic nerve-T cell interactions (neuroimmune crosstalk) in pancreatic cancer and targets this pathway for immunotherapy.
summary_ja: 膵管がん（PDAC）は、緻密な細胞外マトリックス（ECM）とストレス誘発性の神経免疫相互作用を特徴とし、これがT細胞の疲弊と免疫療法の低効果を招いている。本研究では、β遮断薬（カルベジロール）と抗TIM-3抗体（aTIM-3）を共封入した、超音波応答性のバイオミメティックナノキャリア（CT@SM）を開発した。超音波照射によりECMが破壊され、腫瘍深部で放出されたカルベジロールがノルアドレナリンによるT細胞疲弊を緩和し、aTIM-3がM2型腫瘍随伴マクロファージを抑制する。ストレスを負荷したPDACマウスモデルにおいて、このシステムはT細胞を再活性化し、腫瘍成長を顕著に抑制した。
summary_en: To overcome stress-induced neuroimmune immunosuppression and dense extracellular matrix in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), researchers developed an ultrasound-responsive biomimetic nanocarrier co-delivering a β-blocker (carvedilol) and anti-TIM-3 antibody. Ultrasound-triggered cavitation disrupted the tumor matrix and released the drugs, where carvedilol relieved norepinephrine-mediated T cell exhaustion and anti-TIM-3 suppressed immunosuppressive macrophages. This dual-targeting approach significantly enhanced immunotherapy efficacy and suppressed tumor growth in a stressed PDAC mouse model.
key_finding_ja: 超音波応答性ナノキャリアを用いてβ遮断薬と抗TIM-3抗体を共届けることで、ストレス誘発性の神経免疫相互作用（ノルアドレナリンによるT細胞疲弊）を遮断し、膵がんマウスモデルにおける免疫療法の効果を大幅に向上させた。
why_it_matters_ja: ストレスが関与する難治性がんにおいて、神経系と免疫系の相互作用を標的としたナノドラッグデリバリーシステムは、新たな治療戦略として期待される。

title: Engineered Extracellular Vesicles As a New Delivery Platform for Migraine.
abstract: Migraine represents a complex neurovascular disorder that is challenging to treat due to the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and complex pathophysiology involving the trigeminovascular system, neuroinflammation, and cortical spreading depression. Current systemic therapies, including calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) inhibitors, offer benefits but have limited efficacy and may cause adverse effects; thus, highlighting the need for targeted delivery across the BBB. This review introduces extracellular vesicles (EVs) as an appropriate pharmaceutical engineering platform to address such challenges. While traditional treatments have inherent disadvantages, engineered EVs offer efficient blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, targeted delivery, and multi-therapeutic payload capacity for migraine-associated neural circuits. We introduce a framework for pathophysiology-informed technology by first discussing the role of native EVs in promoting the migraine cascade to identify specific sites of therapeutic intervention. In this review, the focus is on pharmaceutical nanotechnology, starting with the strategic selection of producer cells, including "Hijack & Modify" vs De Novo Design, and continuing through sequential nano-engineering of EVs by surface functionalization and utilization of hybrid vesicles for targeting the BBB and trigeminovascular systems to state-of-the-art smart-release systems. We continue with the critical analytical and manufacturing sciences needed to translate such engineered EVs from bench to bedside, addressing important translational challenges through scalable Good manufacturing practices (GMP) production, supported potency assays, and comprehensive quality assurance processes. These include potency tests, GMP production, and robust quality control that may be expanded. Finally, we combine all of these into a single translational pathway that examines the regulatory issues, the patent landscape, and the future of personalized EV therapeutics. The current review provides an exhaustive framework for developing EV-based treatments by combining cutting-edge pharmaceutical nanotechnology with deep biological insights to make migraine treatment more reliable.
authors: Subramony A, Patel VK, Syam Kumar S, Nair SC.
screening_reason: The review discusses engineered extracellular vesicles for migraine therapy, addressing key pathophysiological targets including neuroinflammation.
summary_ja: 片頭痛は、血液脳関門（BBB）や神経炎症、三叉神経血管系が関与する複雑な病態生理のため、治療が困難な神経血管疾患です。本総説では、BBBを透過して標的治療薬を届けるための新たなプラットフォームとして、工学的に改変された細胞外小胞（EV）を紹介しています。EVの生産細胞の選択から、表面修飾、スマート放出システム、さらにGMP製造や品質管理に至るまでの技術的枠組みを網羅しています。これにより、基礎研究から臨床応用へのトランスレーショナルな経路を提示しています。
summary_en: Migraine is a complex neurovascular disorder that is difficult to treat due to the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and neuroinflammation. This review introduces engineered extracellular vesicles (EVs) as a promising pharmaceutical platform for targeted drug delivery across the BBB to migraine-associated neural circuits. It covers the entire development pipeline, including EV engineering strategies, scalable GMP manufacturing, quality control, and regulatory pathways.
key_finding_ja: 工学的に改変された細胞外小胞（EV）は、血液脳関門を効果的に透過し、片頭痛に関連する神経回路へ治療薬を標的輸送するための有望なプラットフォームとなり得ます。
why_it_matters_ja: 従来の全身投与療法における制限を克服し、より効果的で副作用の少ない個別化された片頭痛治療法の開発につながる可能性があります。

title: EXPRESS: Haemorrhage, Hypercoagulability, and Ischaemia: Evolution of Brain Injury after Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Haemorrhage.
abstract: Aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (aSAH) is a catastrophic cerebrovascular event associated with high early mortality and substantial long-term disability. Delayed cerebral ischaemia (DCI) is among its most severe complications and a principal driver of secondary neurological injury. Despite decades of research describing diverse pathophysiological mechanisms, a unifying framework for DCI pathogenesis is still lacking, and its clinical prediction remains challenging. We therefore conducted a narrative review to synthesise current understanding of the spatiotemporal evolution of brain injury following aSAH, with emphasis on integrating mechanisms across overlapping clinical phases. Acute phase events from physical effects of bleeding, including intracranial pressure elevation, hyperacute vasospasm, and microvascular thrombosis, sets off the evolution of downstream brain injuries. During the early phase, converging mechanisms such as neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, spreading depolarisation, and blood-brain barrier disruption coalesce into pan-vascular dysfunction and systemic hypercoagulability. Rather than representing a singular vasospastic complication, these processes collectively evolve into pathobiological states characterised by large-artery vasospasm, microvascular constriction, diffuse capillary occlusion, and supply-demand mismatch, ultimately precipitating DCI and cortical infarction. This review examines the key mechanisms underlying these aforementioned processes and aims to establish mechanistic continuity across the evolving phases of injury following aSAH.
authors: Wang Y, Fisker J, Mishra L, Anstey MH.
journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
screening_reason: The review synthesizes the mechanisms of brain injury after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, highlighting neuroinflammation as a key driver.
summary_ja: 破裂脳動脈瘤によるくも膜下出血（aSAH）後の脳損傷の時空間的進展、特に遅発性脳虚血（DCI）の病態生理に関する文献レビューを行った。急性期における頭蓋内圧上昇や微小血管血栓症などの物理的影響が、その後の神経炎症、酸化ストレス、皮質拡延現象、血液脳関門破綻を引き起こす。これらの多様なプロセスが相互に作用し、大動脈攣縮や微小血管収縮、びまん性毛細血管閉塞を伴う病態へと移行し、最終的にDCIや皮質梗塞を誘発する。本レビューは、aSAH後の各傷害フェーズにおける一連の病態メカニズムを統合的な枠組みとして整理している。
summary_en: This narrative review synthesizes the current understanding of the spatiotemporal evolution of brain injury following aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH), with a focus on delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI). It describes how acute events like intracranial pressure elevation and microvascular thrombosis trigger early-phase processes including neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and blood-brain barrier disruption. These converging mechanisms collectively evolve into pan-vascular dysfunction and capillary occlusion, ultimately precipitating DCI and cortical infarction.
key_finding_ja: くも膜下出血後の脳損傷は、急性期の物理的ストレスから神経炎症や血液脳関門破綻を伴う早期フェーズを経て、最終的に遅発性脳虚血へと至る連続的な病態プロセスとして進行する。
why_it_matters_ja: くも膜下出血後の遅発性脳虚血の複雑な発症機序を統合的に理解することは、より効果的な臨床予測や多角的な治療介入法の確立に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Dapagliflozin ameliorates Alzheimer's disease in rats via stimulating the protective arm of renin angiotensin system and suppressing neuroinflammation.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is associated with renin angiotensin system (RAS) overactivation that stimulates amyloid β-induced neurodegeneration. Activation of angiotensin II type 1 (AT 1 ) receptor impairs the protective phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt) pathway. The combination between angiotensin converting enzyme 2 (ACE2)/ angiotensin 1-7 (Ang 1-7) /Mas receptor (MAS1) axis activation and PI3K/Akt stimulation counteracts AT 1 -induced apoptosis. Dapagliflozin (DAPA) alters the imbalance between the two RAS arms favoring the protective arm. Accordingly, the aim of the current study was to evaluate the possible neuroprotective effects of DAPA in guarding against scopolamine (SCO)-induced AD in rats via inhibiting RAS classical arm, and activating RAS protective arm, as well as PI3K/Akt pathway. DAPA administration suppressed ACE expression and reduced the levels of Ang II and AT 1 in the hippocampi, while elevated the hippocampal levels of ACE2 and Ang 1-7 in addition to boosting MAS1 hippocampal expression. Of note, DAPA prominently augmented the level of PI3K. Also it enhanced the activity of protein kinase A. Furthermore, the hippocampal levels of caspase-3, cytochrome-c, interleukin-6 and nuclear factor kappa B were suppressed, while guanine nucleotide-binding protein alpha-3 level was elevated by DAPA administration. DAPA also attenuated the histopathological SCO-induced damage in rats and enhanced their recognition memory and learning in novel object recognition test and Y-maze spontaneous alternation test. Hence, the current results represent the first evidence for proving that DAPA-induced activation of the protective RAS arm suppressed the cognitive deficits in SCO-induced AD in rats.
authors: Awwad ZM.
screening_reason: The study evaluates the neuroprotective effects of dapagliflozin in a rat model of Alzheimer's disease, focusing on its ability to suppress neuroinflammation.
summary_ja: スコポラミン誘発性アルツハイマー病（AD）ラットモデルを用いて、ダパグリフロジン（DAPA）の神経保護効果とその作用機序を評価した。DAPAの投与は、海馬における古典的レニン・アンジオテンシン系（RAS）を抑制する一方で、保護的RAS（ACE2/Ang 1-7/MAS1）軸およびPI3K/Akt経路を活性化した。さらに、炎症性サイトカインやアポトーシス関連因子の発現を抑制し、組織学的損傷を軽減するとともに、認知機能や学習能力を向上させた。本研究は、DAPAが保護的RAS軸の活性化を介してADの認知機能低下を抑制することを示す初の証拠を提示している。
summary_en: This study evaluated the neuroprotective effects of dapagliflozin (DAPA) in a rat model of scopolamine-induced Alzheimer's disease. DAPA administration suppressed the classical renin-angiotensin system (RAS) arm while activating the protective RAS arm (ACE2/Ang 1-7/MAS1) and the PI3K/Akt pathway in the hippocampus. Additionally, DAPA reduced neuroinflammatory and apoptotic markers, attenuated histopathological damage, and improved learning and memory in the rats.
key_finding_ja: ダパグリフロジンは、保護的レニン・アンジオテンシン系軸およびPI3K/Akt経路の活性化を介して神経炎症やアポトーシスを抑制し、アルツハイマー病モデルラットの認知機能を改善した。
why_it_matters_ja: 糖尿病治療薬であるダパグリフロジンがレニン・アンジオテンシン系の調整を介して神経保護作用を示す可能性が示されたことで、アルツハイマー病に対するドラッグリポジショニングの新たな選択肢となることが期待される。

title: Entropy-Guided Sample-Specific Feature Selection for Robust Incomplete Multi-Omics Learning in Gut Microbiome Disease Prediction and Biomarker Discovery.
abstract: The rapid advancement of multi-omics integration facilitates deep insights into complex diseases. However, incomplete modalities, heterogeneity, and high dimensionality hinder robust analysis. To address these limitations, we propose entropy-guided sample-specific feature selection for robust incomplete multi-omics learning (ESSFS-IMO), a novel framework for accurate disease prediction and interpretable biomarker discovery under missing-data conditions. It combines instance-wise feature selection, entropy-adaptive optimization, and variational representation learning. Specifically, a Gumbel-Softmax-based selector performs per-sample differentiable feature selection, guided by an entropy-based annealing strategy that dynamically adjusts selection sharpness. Selected features are integrated via an information-bottlenecked variational backbone with variance-weighted fusion, enabling robust classification despite missing modalities. Experiments on inflammatory bowel disease datasets demonstrate that ESSFS-IMO outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in accuracy, F1-score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. The model maintains high performance across missing patterns and yields biologically coherent biomarkers, effectively linking microbial, transcriptional, and metabolic profiles to immune regulation. In conclusion, ESSFS-IMO provides a robust, interpretable solution for incomplete multi-omics learning. By integrating entropy-guided selection and variational information bottlenecks, it achieves superior predictive power and resilience while identifying meaningful signatures associated with intestinal inflammation, holding promise for broader biomedical applications.
authors: Li M, Cheng K, Lou M, Wang P, Xu W.
journal: Omics : a journal of integrative biology
screening_reason: The paper proposes a novel machine learning framework specifically designed for disease prediction and biomarker discovery using gut microbiome multi-omics data.
summary_ja: 著者らは、不完全なマルチオミクスデータを用いて頑健な疾患予測とバイオマーカー探索を行うための新しい機械学習フレームワーク「ESSFS-IMO」を開発した。このフレームワークは、エントロピー制御によるサンプル固有の特徴量選択と変分表現学習を組み合わせることで、データの欠損に対応している。炎症性腸疾患のデータセットに適用したところ、高い予測精度を示し、微生物や代謝プロファイルに関連する生物学的に一貫したバイオマーカーを特定することに成功した。
summary_en: The authors developed ESSFS-IMO, a novel machine learning framework designed for robust disease prediction and biomarker discovery using incomplete multi-omics data. The framework integrates entropy-guided sample-specific feature selection with variational representation learning to handle missing modalities. When applied to inflammatory bowel disease datasets, it demonstrated superior predictive accuracy and successfully identified biologically coherent biomarkers linking microbial and metabolic profiles.
key_finding_ja: 欠損のあるマルチオミクスデータから高精度に疾患予測とバイオマーカー特定を行う新手法「ESSFS-IMO」が開発され、炎症性腸疾患データにおいてその有効性が実証された。
why_it_matters_ja: 臨床データに多く見られるデータの欠損や高次元性といった課題を克服し、腸内細菌叢を含むマルチオミクス解析を通じた個別化医療の進展に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Disease-modifying effects on chronic axon damage and white matter degeneration with 4-aminopyridine after acute traumatic brain injury.
abstract: Axonal injury is a hallmark pathology of acute traumatic brain injury (TBI) that drives degeneration of white matter in chronic TBI and in neurodegenerative diseases. No available therapies effectively treat damaged axons. We focused on early, potentially reversible, axonal pathologies of abnormal nodes of Ranvier and demyelination as intervention targets. 4-Aminopyridine (4-AP), which blocks potassium Kv channels, is an FDA-approved drug prescribed for multiple sclerosis to enhance axon signal conduction through nodes with Kv channels exposed by demyelination. We hypothesized that early 4-AP treatment after acute TBI could mitigate secondary axon damage and white matter degeneration. Adult male and female mice received a non-penetrating TBI or sham procedure. A low clinically relevant dose of 4-AP (0.5 mg/kg, b.i.d.) or saline vehicle was initiated at 24 h, administered over 4 weeks, then discontinued for 6-weeks prior to analysis at 10 weeks post-injury. TBI caused atrophy of corpus callosum (CC) white matter and increased serum neurofilament light (NfL) protein, a translational biomarker of axonal injury. 4-AP treatment after injury significantly attenuated CC atrophy and lowered serum NfL levels. 4-AP also significantly lessened CC myelin and oligodendrocyte loss while dampening neuroinflammation, i.e. astrogliosis and microgliosis. In a parallel electron microscopy study, 4-AP reduced intra-axonal structural damage and mitochondrial swelling, normalized axon diameters, and increased myelin thickness. These findings reveal 4-AP disease-modifying effects on the progression of evolving TBI pathology that endure long after discontinuing treatment. More broadly, these results demonstrate proof-of-concept support for developing interventions to treat axon damage and white matter degeneration.
authors: Radomski KL, Zi X, Sullivan GM, Armstrong RC.
journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
screening_reason: The paper evaluates the therapeutic effects of 4-aminopyridine on traumatic brain injury, demonstrating that it dampens neuroinflammation.
summary_ja: 急性外傷性脳損傷（TBI）後の二次的な軸索損傷および白質変性に対する4-アミノピリジン（4-AP）の治療効果をマウスモデルで検証した。TBI誘発の24時間後から4週間にわたり低用量の4-APを投与したところ、治療終了から6週間経過した時点でも脳梁の萎縮や血清ニューロフィラメント軽鎖（NfL）の上昇が有意に抑制されていた。また、4-AP投与は髄鞘やオリゴデンドロサイトの消失を軽減し、アストログリオーシスやマイクログリオーシスなどの神経炎症を抑制した。電子顕微鏡解析では、軸索内の構造的損傷やミトコンドリアの膨張の減少、髄鞘の厚さの維持が確認された。
summary_en: This study investigated the therapeutic effects of early 4-aminopyridine (4-AP) treatment on secondary axonal damage and white matter degeneration in a mouse model of acute traumatic brain injury (TBI). Initiating a low dose of 4-AP 24 hours post-injury for 4 weeks significantly attenuated corpus callosum atrophy, reduced serum neurofilament light levels, and lessened myelin and oligodendrocyte loss. Furthermore, 4-AP treatment dampened neuroinflammation and reduced intra-axonal structural damage, demonstrating long-lasting disease-modifying effects.
key_finding_ja: 急性外傷性脳損傷後の早期における4-アミノピリジン投与は、神経炎症を抑制し、軸索および髄鞘の構造的損傷を軽減することで、長期的な白質変性を抑制する。
why_it_matters_ja: 既存の多発性硬化症治療薬である4-アミノピリジンが外傷性脳損傷後の慢性的な軸索変性を防ぐ病態修飾作用を持つ可能性が示され、新たな治療戦略の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Copper-dependent redox remodeling of the actin cytoskeleton regulates renal epithelial cell mechanics.
abstract: Copper is essential for cellular function but can become toxic in excess. Although its redox and enzymatic roles are well established, how copper availability affects cytoskeletal organization and cell mechanics remains unclear. Here, we show that elevated copper availability increases membrane tether force and F-actin anisotropy in HK-2 proximal tubule cells, consistent with actin cytoskeletal remodeling. Co-treatment with the membrane-permeable ROS scavenger Tiron reversed copper-induced ROS accumulation and mechanical changes without affecting cell viability, supporting a ROS-dependent mechanism. Quantitative proteomics and post-translational modification profiling (ProteomeXchange: PXD072220) identified coordinated changes in actin-regulatory proteins, including Rab35, MsrB2, CK2 subunits, and Septin2, together with reduced actin methionine oxidation and copper-sensitive phosphorylation shifts. These findings identify copper-driven redox signaling as a modulator of renal epithelial cell mechanics associated with remodeling of actin-regulatory pathways.
authors: Pompeu P, Soares J, Ávila Dos Santos Í, Pinheiro GM, Damasceno NJ, Domingues RR, Grelle GMRS, Einicker-Lamas M, Pontes B, Valverde RHF.
journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
screening_reason: The paper mechanistically investigates copper-driven post-translational modifications, specifically actin methionine oxidation and phosphorylation shifts.
summary_ja: 銅の過剰供給が尿細管上皮細胞（HK-2）の細胞骨格組織および力学的特性に与える影響を調査した。銅の増加は活性酸素種（ROS）の蓄積を伴い、膜テザー力およびF-アクチンの異方性を上昇させたが、ROS除去剤の投与によりこれらの変化は消失した。定量プロテオミクスおよび翻訳後修飾プロファイリングにより、アクチン制御因子の変化、アクチンのメチオニン酸化の減少、および銅感受性のリン酸化シフトが同定された。本研究は、銅によるレドックスシグナル伝達がアクチン調節経路の再編成を介して腎上皮細胞の力学特性を制御していることを示している。
summary_en: This study investigated how elevated copper availability affects cytoskeletal organization and cell mechanics in HK-2 proximal tubule cells. Copper increased membrane tether force and F-actin anisotropy through a ROS-dependent mechanism, which was reversed by a ROS scavenger. Quantitative proteomics and post-translational modification profiling revealed coordinated changes in actin-regulatory proteins, reduced actin methionine oxidation, and copper-sensitive phosphorylation shifts.
key_finding_ja: 銅によるレドックスシグナル伝達は、アクチンのメチオニン酸化減少やリン酸化シフトなどの翻訳後修飾の変化を伴い、腎上皮細胞のアクチン細胞骨格再編成と力学的特性を制御している。
why_it_matters_ja: 銅の過剰蓄積が引き起こす腎毒性や細胞力学の変化における翻訳後修飾の役割が明らかになったことで、銅関連の腎疾患に対する新たな治療標的の同定につながる可能性がある。

title: Choroid plexus morphological and microstructural changes across inflammatory phenotypes in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Background Growing evidence supports choroid plexus (CP) involvement in MS pathophysiology, but phase-specific associations according to recent inflammatory activity and longitudinal dynamics remain unclear. Objective To characterize CP alterations in MS using volumetric and quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and explore associations with neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration. Methods We analyzed cross-sectional and 2-year longitudinal data from 101 patients with active relapsing MS (RMS), 83 with inactive progressive MS (PMS), and 100 controls, with MS groups stratified by inflammatory activity within the prior year. CP volume, quantitative T1, and magnetization transfer saturation (MTsat) were assessed alongside imaging, serum, and clinical measures, with validation in a second cohort (62 active/357 inactive MS). Results CP volume was increased in both active RMS and inactive PMS and was associated with lower total and cortical brain volumes. Associations with brain microstructural damage were more pronounced in periventricular regions, compatible with a surface-in pattern. Similar associations were observed in controls, suggesting CP volume may reflect processes beyond MS-specific pathology, including physiological factors. Longitudinally, CP volume increased exclusively in active RMS, with faster expansion associated with thalamic atrophy. CP MTsat was associated with cortical and paramagnetic rim lesions in inactive PMS. Conclusion CP enlargement is consistent across MS phases. Longitudinal expansion occurs in active inflammatory disease and is associated with neurodegenerative changes.
authors: Mastantuono M, Cagol A, Ocampo-Pineda M, Lu PJ, Weigel M, Melie-Garcia L, Aldea AA, Yaldizli Ö, Kappos L, Sormani MP, Kuhle J, Magliozzi R, Granziera C.
screening_reason: The paper investigates choroid plexus changes in multiple sclerosis and directly explores their associations with neuroinflammation.
summary_ja: 多発性硬化症（MS）の病態生理における脈絡叢（CP）の関与を評価するため、横断的および2年間の縦断的MRIデータを用いてCPの体積および微細構造の変化を解析した。その結果、活動性再発寛解型MS（RMS）および非活動性進行型MS（PMS）の双方でCP体積の増加が認められ、全脳および皮質体積の減少と関連していた。縦断的解析では、CP体積の増加は活動性RMSでのみ観察され、その急速な拡大は視床萎縮と関連していた。これらの結果は、CPの肥大がMSの病相を通じて一貫して見られ、活動性の炎症期に縦断的な拡大が生じることを示している。
summary_en: This study evaluated choroid plexus (CP) alterations in multiple sclerosis (MS) using cross-sectional and 2-year longitudinal MRI data from patients with active relapsing MS (RMS), inactive progressive MS (PMS), and controls. CP volume was increased in both active RMS and inactive PMS, and its longitudinal expansion occurred exclusively in active RMS, correlating with thalamic atrophy. The findings suggest that CP enlargement is consistent across MS phases, with longitudinal expansion linked to active inflammatory disease and neurodegeneration.
key_finding_ja: 脈絡叢の体積増加は多発性硬化症の各病相で一貫して観察され、特に活動性再発寛解型において縦断的な拡大と神経変性変化との関連が示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 脈絡叢の形態変化が多発性硬化症の炎症活動性や神経変性のバイオマーカーとして機能する可能性があり、今後の病態モニタリングへの応用が期待される。

title: Deep Learning Prediction of O-Glycopeptide Tandem Mass Spectra Enhances O-Glycoproteomics.
abstract: Protein glycosylation, a post-translational modification involving the attachment of glycans to proteins, plays critical roles in numerous physiological and pathological cellular functions. Characterization of protein glycosylation is one of the most challenging problems due to the high heterogeneity of glycosites and glycan structures. Recently, deep learning has been adopted to predict N-glycopeptide tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) spectra and exhibited a promising effect in N-glycoproteomics analysis. However, current deep learning frameworks struggle to accurately predict O-glycopeptide MS/MS spectra due to the complexity of O-glycopeptides and the limited availability of training data. In this study, we introduce DeepGPO, a deep learning framework for the prediction of O-glycopeptide MS/MS spectra. The DeepGPO incorporates a Transformer module alongside two graph neural network modules designed for handling branched glycans. To address the issue of data scarcity in O-glycoproteomics, various training methods are adopted in DeepGPO, such as the introduction of training weights for different MS/MS spectra and the adoption of pre-training strategies. With the predicted MS/MS, O-glycosylation sites can be localized even in the absence of site-determining ions. Currently, DeepGPO supports both mono- and double-O-glycosylated peptides. It shows promising application in clinical human O-glycoproteomics. We anticipate that DeepGPO will inspire future advancements in glycoproteomics research.
authors: Zong Y, Wang Y, Qiao L.
screening_reason: The paper presents a deep learning framework for O-glycoproteomics, which is directly related to the study of protein post-translational modifications.
summary_ja: タンパク質のO-糖鎖修飾は重要な翻訳後修飾ですが、その構造の多様性とデータ不足から、質量分析（MS/MS）スペクトルの正確な予測は困難でした。本研究では、O-糖鎖ペプチドのMS/MSスペクトルを予測するディープラーニングフレームワーク「DeepGPO」を開発しました。DeepGPOは、Transformerモジュールと分岐糖鎖を扱う2つのグラフニューラルネットワークを組み込んでいます。このモデルにより、部位決定イオンが存在しない場合でも、O-糖鎖修飾部位の同定が可能になります。
summary_en: O-glycosylation is a key post-translational modification, but predicting O-glycopeptide MS/MS spectra has been challenging due to structural complexity and data scarcity. To address this, researchers developed DeepGPO, a deep learning framework incorporating Transformer and graph neural network modules. DeepGPO enables the localization of O-glycosylation sites even in the absence of site-determining ions, supporting both mono- and double-O-glycosylated peptides.
key_finding_ja: 新たに開発されたディープラーニングフレームワーク「DeepGPO」は、Transformerとグラフニューラルネットワークを用いてO-糖鎖ペプチドのMS/MSスペクトルを高精度に予測し、修飾部位の同定を可能にしました。
why_it_matters_ja: データの希少性や構造の複雑さによる制限を克服することで、臨床におけるヒトO-グライコプロテオミクス解析の進展に貢献することが期待されます。
